title: How many lines of symmetry does a paper star have?
description: Thin coloured paper is folded several times and cut to make an eight pointed star. Counting the folds through its tips and through its dips shows all its lines of symmetry. Keeko's doubt is that the star has only one line of symmetry.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fold and cut pattern can have many lines of symmetry, found through the opposite tips and through the opposite dips. Watch for students who count only the first fold.

source: Make different symmetric shapes by folding and cutting. Use
video_script.why: The child sees that folding more times gives a design with more lines of symmetry, and counts them for an eight pointed star.
video_script.substitution: Count the folds through opposite tips, then the folds through opposite dips.
video_script.anchor: a blue paper star with eight tips, cut from thin coloured paper that was folded several times
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the star has only one line of symmetry, the line of the first fold. Folding the star along other lines also makes the halves match, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The eight pointed star has eight lines of symmetry

final_answer.spoken: the eight pointed star has eight lines of symmetry

maths_rules: Each fold line of the folded paper is a line of symmetry of the opened cut-out
A regular star with 8 tips has 4 lines through pairs of opposite tips
The same star has 4 lines through pairs of opposite dips
The first fold is only one of the lines of symmetry, not the only one
video_script.design: One idea: count the fold lines through the tips and through the dips. The blue star stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: only the first fold line counts.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a strip of thin blue paper folded several times with scissors beside it; an opened blue paper star with eight tips

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.fold: the thin blue paper is folded several times and cut along its edges
marks.star: the opened blue star with eight tips appears
marks.ask: the words find the folds that match appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book, and it is about folding and cutting.
<bookmark mark='fold'/>Thin coloured paper is folded several times, and then it is cut.
<bookmark mark='star'/>When the paper is opened, it shows a star with eight tips.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>On how many folds do the two halves of this star match?

beats.on_screen: the blue star stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the star folds along one line and the two halves cover each other; the fold line glows and the words line of symmetry appear on it

marks.match: the fold line glows and the words line of symmetry appear on it

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>A fold line where both halves cover each other exactly is called a line of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: the star with its 8 pointed tips marked by dots and its 8 inner dips marked by small rings

marks.tips: the eight pointed tips light up one by one
marks.dips: the eight inner dips light up between the tips

beats.colours: tips = blue dots, dips = orange rings
narration: <bookmark mark='tips'/>The star has eight pointed tips.
<bookmark mark='dips'/>Between two tips, there is an inner corner. We call it a dip.

beats.on_screen: Given: an opened star with 8 tips, cut from paper folded several times

marks.given: the facts are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, an opened star has eight tips, and it was cut from paper folded several times.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of lines of symmetry of the star

marks.find: the thing to find is written under Given

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many lines of symmetry the star has.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: fold the star along a line through two opposite tips; the halves cover each other. There are 4 such lines, one for each pair of opposite tips

marks.fold: the star folds along a line through two opposite tips and the halves match
marks.four: four lines through pairs of opposite tips are drawn one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='fold'/>Step one, fold the star along a line through two opposite tips, because the halves should match.
<bookmark mark='four'/>They match, so it is a line of symmetry. Eight tips make four such pairs, so there are four lines.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: fold the star along a line through two opposite dips; the halves cover each other. There are 4 such lines

marks.fold: the star folds along a line through two opposite dips and the halves match
marks.four: four lines through pairs of opposite dips are drawn one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='fold'/>Step two, fold the star along a line through two opposite dips, because these folds can match too.
<bookmark mark='four'/>The halves match again. Eight dips also make four pairs, so there are four more lines.

marks.add: the four blue lines and the four orange lines are added: 4 + 4 = 8

beats.colours: tip lines = blue, dip lines = orange
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the lines, because every line must be counted once. Four and four make eight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: the star has 8 lines of symmetry

marks.ans: the answer is boxed and all eight lines glow on the star

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The eight pointed star has eight lines of symmetry.
Each fold of the paper became one of these lines.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the star
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says only one line; the star is folded along a second line and the halves match again; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears with the words only one line
marks.fix: the star folds along a second line, the halves match and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the star has only one line of symmetry, the line of the first fold.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But fold the star along another line, and the halves match again.
The first fold is only one of its lines, so there are more to find.
